name: Nairobi
tagline: Safari Capital with Year-Round Spring Weather and a Booming Tech Scene
description: Nairobi is East Africa's most dynamic city, offering FIRE retirees a unique combination of urban sophistication, wildlife literally at the city's edge, and a surprisingly strong expat infrastructure. The climate at 5,500 feet elevation is perpetual spring. English is an official language and widely spoken. Private healthcare is solid and affordable, the food scene blends Kenyan, Indian, and international cuisines, and Nairobi National Park means you can watch lions with the city skyline as a backdrop. Kenya's growing tech hub, dubbed Silicon Savannah, gives the city a forward-looking energy.

quickFacts.visa: eVisa required for US citizens (90 days, renewable). No dedicated retirement visa. Residence permits available through investment ($100K+) or as a person of independent means with sufficient passive income.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – exercise caution, especially at night; secure compounds recommended
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical highland with mild temperatures year-round

housing.description: Secure but basic 1BR in a gated Kilimani or Lavington block — safety premium is non-negotiable

dining.description: Local nyama-choma/Indian joints and kibandas a few times a week

healthcare.description: Basic local private cover, single adult 45–55, inpatient-focused

transportation.description: Bolt/Uber for everyday trips — safer than self-driving

1M.lifestyle: A secure, gated 1BR in Kilimani or Lavington — the safety premium is non-negotiable in Nairobi, so the compound guard and walls come standard. Most meals are cooked from cheap, excellent local produce, with nyama-choma and Indian spots for eating out a few times a week. You skip self-driving in favor of Bolt and Uber, which is safer and simpler in the traffic. Cover is a real but basic local private plan, inpatient-focused. A neighborhood gym and the odd cinema or bar fill the discretionary slack, and the highland climate means no heating or cooling bills.

2M.lifestyle: A nicer furnished 1BR in buzzy Westlands or leafy Kilimani, dining out several evenings a week including mid-range restaurants. Comprehensive local insurance (Jubilee, AAR, or Britam) now covers outpatient visits too, not just hospital stays. You lean on ride-hail heavily or run a modest small car. A mid-range gym plus nightlife and weekend outings keep things social — unstressed but not lavish.

3M.lifestyle: A serviced 1BR or compact 2BR-for-one in a prime area like Westlands, Riverside, Kilimani, or Lavington, where security, housekeeping, and backup power are bundled into the rent. You eat well and often, carry a strong private plan with high limits and medical-evacuation cover, and travel most months — a Maasai Mara safari lodge or a Diani-coast weekend. Transport is frictionless: unlimited Bolt/Uber plus a hired driver when you want one, or a comfortable owned car.

5M.lifestyle: Upper-crust solo living — a furnished Runda or Karen cottage, or a Riverside penthouse, kept by a part-time housekeeper and a part-time driver. You dine out almost daily including Nairobi's top restaurants and hotel venues, carry a genuine top-tier international plan, and belong to a private club. A standalone house means a generator, borehole, security, and pool upkeep, all handled. Safari, coast, and regional travel are routine — unmistakably affluent, yet still one person's footprint.

10M.lifestyle: The ceiling of what one person can meaningfully consume in Nairobi — a luxury furnished house in Karen or Runda, kept deliberately below the ambassadorial-mansion scale, run by full-time staff scaled to one home: a live-in housekeeper/cook, a driver, and day-and-night guarding. Dining ranges from top hotel restaurants to private-chef nights, and international concierge cover gives full global access with evacuation. A large house runs on full power with backup generator, borehole, pool, and security, and the discretionary budget funds clubs, first-class travel, golf, and sailing. It sits far below a family compound — no household-of-four food or staffing, no estate.
